## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [7. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.69
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.69
- Datum: 7.12.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
7 XII 1940 Dear Hannah and Manfred, we have a letter from
Eva today that she has for 4 weeks no news from you, I am afraid
that letters have been lost. We wrote to you both every week regularly
and now being anxious we have tried to make an arrangement with
the Western Telegraf that all the telegramms we send could be paid by
you as we want to inform you regularly about your daughter and
are somewhat short of money. You will understand that and I hope it
will be possible so that you may not have to add your other anxious
fimes the worry about your child. Please send us like before cables
from time to time - we are in such an enormous distance that letters
are not sufficient as they seem to take much time. Eva writes quite
happy, she is somewhat disappointed that we arrive later than we
proposed but I want badly a few weeks without travelling. From us
there is nothing new to relate. We live a retired life and till now
we could stand the heat very well, only one wants more sleep and
feels his energy a little diminished. We our selves have no letters from
you all now for three weeks but your cable reassured us at least
that you are allright. Kindest regards to all and love to you
Rio, Hotel Central. Stefan Zweig

Dear Hanna & Manfred, - There seems to be an all-round
shortage of letters just now - we have no letters from you since
3 weeks you have no letter from Eva for 5 weeks and she has no
letter from you since 4 weeks. But I hope that all these letters
which certainly have been written are not lost but only de-
layed and will arrive as a nice Christmas surprise. In any
case I repeat our birthday wishes which we expressed in our last
letter. - We are all-right, it is not yet so very hot and I
have not even started bathing. We are continuing to work.
and to see few people, and my only activity consists in
taking Spanish lessons, in order to change my Esperanto
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelblichem Papier. Die erste Seite enthält zwei Abschnitte, der zweite beginnt nach dem Absatz.

pages.transcription:
2)
into real Spanish. From Eva we had another letter
to-day telling that she has seen Rose Wohl and her sister and
brother-in-law and that they are "very sweet". But I have
had no word from Rose herself - it seems to be a general
defect of the American character, this not-writing - although I
feel sure of her friendship and very best intentions. Only my
sister-in-law is reliable and I am beginning to appreciate
it very much. She wrote a few days ago that she had again
spoken to Eva by phone and that everything was allright
and that she was going to see her soon. I am looking forward
to seeing Eva in February. Even if we do not remain in
Newyork, we will not be more than two hours away at the
most, and I shall be able to see her frequently for at
least 2 or 3 months. To make plans or even to think ahead
for more than 4 or 5 months one does not dare although I
always hope for pleasant events and sometimes even have
rather premature dreams about being at home again with you.
I am surprised to find myself so much more sentimental
than I thought, but I discover more and more how deeply
this habit of living with you for so long, has grown and how
much I miss you. My only consolation is that at least
our house is useful to you as a place for rest and I
do wish it will remain it. How are Raumann fitting
in that Rosemount-life? Give them my kindest regards,
also to all the others especially to Livy and Ursula
to whom I want to write since a long time.
Best wishes, kisses and souvenirs,
Lotte

pages.notes: Rückseite des zweiten Blattes mit aufgelegter Farb- und Grauskala zur Archivierung.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Stefan Zweig und Lotte Zweig ist klar und deutlich.
